payload.title: hyp prints the /goal prompt for any Goal from the log, and a Goal body carries the run's constraints
payload.body:
Builds `hyp prompt` for issue #113: hyp prints the /goal prompt for any Goal from the log, and a Goal body carries the run's constraints under May change:, Read only: and Never:. The candidate is a hyp commit. go test is the instrument, and skillcheck decides the skill text.
Done means, by the owner on 2026-11-11: for a Goal with a valid block, the prompt carries every clause the hand-written run-5 prompt had, except the actor, the owner's answer, the branch, the PR, the commit and the run's own plan. A test pins this on a synthetic Goal under internal/cli/testdata. checkpoint-store:G-D1CH1R has no block, so hyp prompt refuses it and no test compares it.
The session settled that hyp prompt is a command that reads the log, and that no skill writes the prompt.
May change: the hyp repository, by commits on the local branch feat/goal-prompt and then a PR that the run opens and never merges
May change: cmd, internal, the docs and a new ADR 0022
May change: skills, for the descriptions of hyp-goal-run and hyp-prototype that name one kind of Goal, the hand-off of hyp-owner-grill, and a build-Goal review round in hyp-goal-run
Read only: the existing ADRs, every other tree under investigations, and recipes
Never: replace the installed hyp binary
Never: edit an existing ADR or a Goal
Never: merge a PR or close #113 (write Part of #113)

lines.text: [P] For a Goal with a valid constraints block, `hyp prompt G --actor A` exits 0 and prints, each ending in a newline and in this order: the store's absolute root, A, the Goal's display id, `hyp-goal-run`, the stop clauses (the runner owes nothing; N non-retracted Results recorded under A in this Goal, N being 5 by default; it cannot take the next step honestly and says why), then the block's lines byte for byte. With no flag there is no branch or PR clause.

[P] `--experiments N` sets N. `--branch B` and `--pr N` each add exactly one clause after the block, and each clause only narrows what the block allows. The output is the same for any order of the flags.

[N] A body's block runs from its first line that starts with `May change:`, `Read only:` or `Never:` to the end, and is valid only if all three headings appear, each has text after it, and every non-empty line starts with one (headings are case-sensitive; a line of spaces, a tab or a lone carriage return is not empty). For a body with no valid block, `hyp prompt` exits 1, names the missing heading or the bad line, and prints no prompt on stdout.

[P] `hyp add goal` with a body that has a heading but no valid block succeeds and warns on stderr, naming the rule; a body with no heading adds without a warning. Replay and `hyp check` report no error for either Goal.
[N] `hyp prompt` writes nothing: the bytes of `.tree` are the same before and after. It carries no owner answer and no tree state beyond the Goal's id and body.

[N] These exit 2: a missing or invalid actor, a branch that git refuses (such as one with a space), `--pr` or `--experiments` below 1, a repeated flag, an unknown node, and a node that is not a Goal. A run where no `.tree` is found exits 3.

[N] In a store with two Goals, `hyp prompt` reads only the named Goal's body: the other Goal's block never appears in the output, and a Goal without a valid block is refused while the other Goal prints.
[N] `hyp prompt` exits 1, naming the actor, when the actor already has a Result under that Goal.

why: Owner flow, issue #113: the run's constraints get a recorded place and hyp prints the /goal prompt from the log. Written after the grill of 2026-11-12, with the owner's approval of this command.

payload.title: Design record: hyp prompt is a command that reads the log
payload.body: Records the one design question of issue #113 that the owner settled by argument in the grill session of 2026-11-12: where the /goal prompt is produced. The rivals are a hyp command that reads the log and a skill that writes the prompt from hyp show. The session is the evidence; no run was made. It has no lines: no run checks its candidates, and its cases are the lines of the build Goal G-VRG6SA, which builds this design.

why: Owner flow, issue #113: a design settled by argument is its own Goal, apart from the build Goal G-VRG6SA. Written after the grill of 2026-11-12, with the owner's approval of this command.
